title: The Impact of ESG Investments on Market Capitalization
content: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) investing has gained prominence as investors seek sustainable value creation alongside financial returns. This review systematically examines the relationship between ESG performance and firm market capitalization, addressing the question of whether high ESG ratings translate into tangible financial advantages. Employing a PRISMA 2020-guided systematic literature review, ten empirical studies published between 2020 and 2025 were analyzed across multiple sectors and global regions. The methodology included structured database searches (Scopus, Web of Science, SSRN, ScienceDirect), predefined inclusion/exclusion criteria, and thematic synthesis. Results indicate a general trend of positive correlation between ESG scores and market capitalization, particularly in regulated sectors (e.g., energy, finance) and developed markets with stronger ESG regulatory frameworks. ESG performance also appears to enhance firm resilience during crises, such as the COVID-19 pandemic. However, rating inconsistencies and greenwashing remain significant challenges, often obscuring the link between reported ESG performance and real sustainability practices. The review concludes that ESG is a financially material factor, but its valuation impact is highly context-dependent. It calls for standardized ESG metrics, longitudinal impact assessments, and greater transparency to ensure ESG investing fulfills its promise of aligning financial markets with sustainability goals.
